name: the fence never opens, so a tag QUOTED inside a code block is reported as live
expect: a tag inside a COLUMN-0 fence is NOT flagged

name: the fence swallows the REST of the document instead of just its own body
expect: ...but a tag AFTER that fence closes is still flagged

name: an INDENTED fence is treated as opening one, so a live tag beneath it is hidden
leading whitespace stops being allowed, so an indented tag the parser DID assemble walks through
expect: an INDENTED tag OUTSIDE a fence is caught

name: the end anchor is dropped from the tag grammar, so prose FOLLOWING a tag reads as a tag
expect: a tag with trailing prose is NOT a tag

name: the mutations tag stops being checked — half the retired grammar goes unfenced
expect: a standalone mutations tag is caught

name: audit reports NOTHING visited, so the corpus size claim is hollow
expect: the scanned count is the number of documents READ

name: an unreadable document is silently skipped — a file it could not check reads as clean [anchor re-bound r2: the fix moved this line]
edits:
findings.append(Finding(str(md), 0, f"could not be read, so it was NOT checked: {exc}",
                                    unreadable=True))
expect: an undecodable document is reported, not silently skipped

name: the guard imitates the reader's line-splitter instead of using it (splitlines vs split)
edits: for n, line in enumerate(text.split("\n"), start=1):
for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
expect: a 0xb before a fence does not open one — extract() splits on '\n' alone, and assembles this tag

name: the narrowed-corpus refusal is dropped, so reading a SUBSET reads as a clean run
edits:
missing = want - seen
    stray = seen - want
expect: ...but reading a SUBSET is CANNOT RUN, not a pass

name: the shortfall check fires ALWAYS, so a complete scan is refused too (unfalsifiable both ways)
expect: a full-tree scan has no shortfall

name: an unreadable doc is dropped from the VISITED set, so it reads as a NARROWED corpus (r2 H1)
expect: ...so it is ACCOUNTED FOR and does not read as a narrowing

name: every finding claims to be unreadable, so a narrowed corpus excuses itself per tag
expect: a TAG finding is not marked unreadable

name: the guard compares CARDINALITY instead of identity, so a same-size different tree passes (Codex r2 High)
edits: missing = set() if len(seen) == len(want) else want - seen
expect: ...and a same-SIZE but different set is refused — the property is which documents were read, not how many
